behavior.before: initializeSigningNamespace left access=nil; refresh/reconcile/finalize exposed a real publication but did not reconnect the same session, leaving Settings pairing/prepare disabled until lifecycle bootstrap.
behavior.after: Every actual published lease passes one shared reconnect helper while the existing busy ownership is held. It discards old signing state, invokes the normal resolve(configuration) full current-Bundle/Vault path and publishes the actual existing journal phase before Owner synchronization.
behavior.accountFinalizationFailure: Even if the account final save fails after a real Vault publication, reconnect is attempted using that fact; the original account error is still thrown. DeveloperMaterialFinalizationFailure keeps the published observation and an independent optional connectionError.
behavior.expiredOrUnusableInstalledApplication: A known cryptographic/material refusal with no unexpected recovery context retains the actual publication but cannot grant signing. This preserves the existing explicit expired-enrollment behavior.
behavior.unknownRecoveryContext: Only nil or Coordinator.invalidRecoveryContext is an expected absent recovery context in this local helper. Any other context remains an error with the publication; no global classification changes.
behavior.cancelStorageUnknownFailure: The old connection is discarded first. Cancellation, storage, unknown errors or a failed status ACK still throw with the acknowledged publication retained; lost status ACK cannot retain signing access.
behavior.concurrency: The original public refresh/reconcile/finalize busy guard stays held across account publication, resolver and status publication. Owner methods keep isWorking until the existing status/recovery/material-error observations are synchronized.
behavior.successfulUnchangedRefreshWrites: Existing publish deduplication remains; no new store or background work is introduced.

newTests.suiteSerialization: Existing @Suite(..., .serialized) and original URLProtocol peer; no new suite or peer registry.
scenarios: Same live Owner becomes signing-ready after first publication without a new foreground/bootstrap.
A changed actual owned current Bundle never gains signing from a real published lease and the publication remains visible.
A one-shot callback fires only after the actual third successful Keychain save, cancels the real worker and checks the persisted publication survives without signing access.
Explicit account finalization reaches the same Owner, restores signing state and never repeats CSR/profile requests.
newTests.testFixtureChanges: FaultStorage gains one locked one-shot after-successful-save observer; callback runs after checked Keychain storage returns, outside its lock. No production hook or timing wait.
